title: coyodex
goal: coyodex builds a map of a codebase that a person can read top down, without reading the code. An AI coding agent follows a written method to read the project and produce that map: diagrams, one plain sentence on every box, and a link to a real file and line under every claim. The map is committed next to the code and served as an interactive browser page. The product exists for one situation: your coding agent wrote a lot of code, the code runs, and you have lost track of what is under your feet. It is for the developer who owns such a project, for the agent that has to keep the map honest, and for whoever maintains the method itself.

roles.name: Map reader
roles.wants: To understand a codebase top down, and to drop into the code only where it matters.
roles.drives: Installs the skill, starts the map server, reads the map, and asks for map changes in plain words.

roles.name: Coding agent
roles.wants: To follow the written method end to end and produce a map every gate accepts.
roles.drives: Runs the briefing, the tree sizing, the fan-out, the merge, every gate, and the change-impact report.

roles.name: coyodex developer
roles.wants: To know whether a change to the method made the maps better or worse.
roles.drives: Archives a map, scores a rebuild against the accepted one, and reviews what a finished build did.

glossary.meaning: The whole picture coyodex produces for a project: diagrams, plain-language text on every box, and code links.
The map as currently accepted, pinned to one commit. A code change is compared against it.
Analysing a project from scratch and producing a new map. Hand edits are thrown away.
The browser page that shows a map. Served live from the map, never committed as a file.
One screen in the viewer answering one question. Happy Path, Features, Entities and Deployment are views.
One thing drawn on a view. A component, an entity, a feature or a dependency each draw as one.
The file and line a box points at. A box without one is an ungrounded claim.
The report saying what a code change does to the map: what is added, changed or gone.
Folding a change-impact report into the baseline and re-pinning it to the new commit.
Your agent wrote a lot of code, and the code still runs. Nobody knows any more what is under your feet.
The written instructions a coding agent follows to build a map. This product's real logic lives there.
The small pointer file installed into each coding agent so a person can invoke coyodex by name.
One worker's slice of a map, written as its own file. Every fragment is merged into the map.
The briefing a fan-out worker is handed, printed by a command so the wording never drifts.
Splitting one phase of a build across many workers who run at the same time and never share context.
A fresh worker handed a batch of the map's claims and told to disprove each one against the code.
One statement the map makes about what the code actually does, carrying the line that witnesses it.
The ranked list of claims the audit says need code evidence. The skeptics work it top down.
The record of how many claims were challenged and how the skeptics voted on each.
A code link pointing at a line that cannot be acting, such as a definition header or a comment.
A finding that never blocks. Fix it, or write one line saying why it is acceptable.
One written line that stops a named advisory firing forever, because a person judged it acceptable.
An automatic check a map must pass. Failing one is a defect in the map, not in the code.
A measurement of the code tree made before the map is drawn: folder weight, symbols, and an expected size.
How many components a tree of this size should produce, derived from the code alone with a band around it.
One module-sized unit of the code, roughly a folder with one purpose. The map's main structural box.
A group of components, and of smaller subsystems. What the first screen of a large map shows.
A real named type in the code that the product stores or reasons about. Drawn with its fields and relations.
A group of entities that belong together. The domain-model twin of a subsystem.
One goal one actor has, with one trigger and one outcome. The unit the product's story is told in.
The inside view of one use case: the ordered steps among components, dependencies and entities.
A named step sequence shared by two or more flows, so shared machinery is written down once.
One end-to-end walk through the use cases that tells the product's story and reaches every actor.
A group of use cases serving one goal of the product. What a product person would call an area.
One decision the product makes, in product words, plus every place the code enforces it.
A group of business rules covering one area a product person would argue about.
A surface the outside world reaches the product through, or a job the product starts on its own.
The commit a map says it describes. Every code link is read at that commit.
Scoring two maps of one project to say whether a change to the method made map quality better or worse.
Reading a finished build and its transcript to find what went wrong in the process.
How an eval rates a new map, in one of three words. Pass means as good as before. Drift means a measurement moved too far. Regressed means a hard check got worse.

use_cases.name: Install the coyodex skill into the coding agents
use_cases.trigger_outcome: The reader runs the install target in a fresh clone. Every coding agent on that machine can now answer to coyodex.

use_cases.name: Start the local map server
use_cases.trigger_outcome: The reader starts the server once. A landing page lists every project that has a map.

use_cases.name: Brief the reader on what will be analysed
use_cases.trigger_outcome: The agent begins a run. The reader sees the file count, what each exclusion removed, and the commit the map will name.

use_cases.name: Declare code the map should not describe
use_cases.trigger_outcome: The reader lists a fixture or vendored tree in the ignore file. Every measurement afterwards drops those files.

use_cases.name: Size the code tree before choosing altitude
use_cases.trigger_outcome: The agent asks for the weight of every folder. The answer gives line counts, churn, a symbol index and an expected size.

use_cases.name: Hand a fan-out worker its contract
use_cases.trigger_outcome: The agent is about to dispatch workers. One command prints the worker's half of the briefing, ready to fill in.

use_cases.name: Self-check one harvested fragment
use_cases.trigger_outcome: A worker finishes its rows. The check reports schema, code-link and drift problems while the worker can still fix them.

use_cases.name: Merge the workers' fragments into one map
use_cases.trigger_outcome: Every fragment is on disk. Merging them writes the map and its readable view, refusing any duplicate identifier.

use_cases.name: Turn path rules into explicit assignments
use_cases.trigger_outcome: The agent knows folder paths, not identifiers. Path rules expand into an assignment file, naming every rule that matched nothing.

use_cases.name: Look up one part of the map
use_cases.trigger_outcome: The agent needs one element's stored record. A read-only lookup returns it, from a finished map or a build fragment.

use_cases.name: Check the map is well formed
use_cases.trigger_outcome: The agent finishes a write. The check reports broken references, bad code links, and every balance and coverage advisory.

use_cases.name: Make the map's two layers refute each other
use_cases.trigger_outcome: The agent has a map that is well formed. The walk and the flows are compared, and the claims needing code evidence are ranked.

use_cases.name: Disprove a claim against the code
use_cases.trigger_outcome: A fresh worker is handed a batch of claims and told to break them. Each comes back confirmed, refuted, or impossible to settle.

use_cases.name: Record what the skeptics proved
use_cases.trigger_outcome: Every verdict file is in. The counts are derived and written into the map, refusing a verdict for a claim nobody pinned.

use_cases.name: Correct a code link that points at the wrong line
use_cases.trigger_outcome: The skeptics report a truer line than the map holds. The correction is written so the next merge keeps it.

use_cases.name: Drop a claim the code refutes
use_cases.trigger_outcome: A relation turns out not to exist. Removing it also heals the walk steps that rode on it.

use_cases.name: Record an advisory the reader accepts
use_cases.trigger_outcome: An advisory is a judgement, not a defect. One line written under the heading it names stops it firing again.

use_cases.name: Re-balance the diagrams against the traced graph
use_cases.trigger_outcome: Grouping was cut before any relation existed. The report shows each screen's box count and where a split would fall.

use_cases.name: Run the pre-commit read
use_cases.trigger_outcome: The agent believes the map is done. One run does every gate, writes the whole finding list to a file, and says which gates ran.

use_cases.name: Stamp which conversation built the map
use_cases.trigger_outcome: The map is written and checked. The session and the minute are recorded, so the transcript can be found again later.

use_cases.name: Open a project's map in a browser
use_cases.trigger_outcome: The reader clicks a project on the landing page. Every view is built from the map on demand and drawn.

use_cases.name: Follow the product's story end to end
use_cases.trigger_outcome: The reader wants to know what the product does. One column shows every feature in the order the story runs.

use_cases.name: Read the code under a box
use_cases.trigger_outcome: The reader wants the evidence behind a claim. The file opens at that line, read from the commit the map names.

use_cases.name: Open an element's source in the editor
use_cases.trigger_outcome: The reader wants to change what a box describes. One click opens that line in the editor or on the hosting site.

use_cases.name: Report what a code change did to the map
use_cases.trigger_outcome: The code has moved past the commit the map names. The report says which parts of the map are added, changed or gone.

use_cases.name: Fold a change report into the map
use_cases.trigger_outcome: The reader says the report is right. The map is patched element by element and re-pinned to the new commit.

use_cases.name: Change the map by asking in plain words
use_cases.trigger_outcome: The reader asks to split, rename, move or drill deeper into a part. The map is edited directly, then put through every gate.

use_cases.name: See what an edit changed, row by row
use_cases.trigger_outcome: The agent has the map from before and after an edit. Every added, dropped and changed row is listed with the fields that moved.

use_cases.name: Score a rebuilt map against the accepted one
use_cases.trigger_outcome: The developer changed the method and rebuilt. The two maps are measured and the run says pass, drift or regressed.

use_cases.name: Have judges read both maps
use_cases.trigger_outcome: Counting cannot say whether the words are true. Judges read both maps for grounding and against a rubric, and their verdicts are gathered.

use_cases.name: Accept a run as the new baseline
use_cases.trigger_outcome: The developer decides the new map is the standard. Its map, view, profile and judgement all become the baseline.

use_cases.name: Measure how many planted falsehoods the skeptics catch
use_cases.trigger_outcome: Refutation rates cannot say whether skeptics are weak. Planting known-false claims gives an answer key to score against.

use_cases.name: Refuse to review a build that has not finished
use_cases.trigger_outcome: A build stamps its session near the end. Reviewing early would read the previous run, so the check stops it.

use_cases.name: Read a build transcript in slices
use_cases.trigger_outcome: A build transcript is far too large to read whole. An index comes first, then one range at a time.

use_cases.name: Score a build's behaviour against the method
use_cases.trigger_outcome: The gates say a map is well formed, never that the agent followed the method. The transcript is scored rule by rule.

use_cases.name: Measure what a build spent
use_cases.trigger_outcome: The developer wants the price of a map. Time and tokens are totalled across every worker, then divided by the rows produced.

use_cases.name: Archive a map so the next run builds from scratch
use_cases.trigger_outcome: A rebuild must never read the map it replaces. Filing the old map away leaves the folder empty and keeps the baseline.

use_cases.name: See the change overlaid on the map
use_cases.trigger_outcome: The reader picks two commits in the viewer. Every box the change reaches is marked, including the ones it reaches indirectly.

components.name: The eval recipe
components.purpose: Written instructions for scoring two maps of the same code. The scoring says whether a change to the coyodex method made maps better or worse. The same instructions fix the quality rubric a reviewer scores against, and the pass marks a map must clear. A run ends in one word: as good, drifted, or worse.

evidence.why: The recipe states its job, which is to compare the current map against an archived one.
The recipe forbids editing either map to improve a number, and voids a run where that happened.
The pass marks hold the hard check that a map must not gain new validation problems.
The rubric names its first quality dimension, asking whether the map's claims match the code.
The recipe hands a caller off to the separate recipe for a provably blind rebuild.

components.name: The build retrospective recipe
components.purpose: Written instructions for reviewing one finished build. The review reads the map the build made and the chat that made it. The review reports the friction, bugs and gaps the build revealed. A review changes nothing on disk, so every finding is a proposal for the developer. Each past finding is re-checked with a command that returns a number.

evidence.why: The recipe states its job, which is to read the map and the chat and report what the run shows.
The recipe forbids changing anything on disk, so every finding stays a proposal.
The recipe orders the reviewer to refuse while the build is still writing.
The recipe collects every promise a method change made since the previous build.
The durable record of past proposals says the recipe must read it before a review starts.

components.name: Map document
components.purpose: Holds the shape of a map: what a box, an arrow and a code link may each contain. Writes the map file the same way every time, so a rebuild shows only real changes. Also holds the word lists the whole tool shares.

evidence.why: The one serializer: fixed key order, indent 2, trailing newline, so the same map always writes identical bytes.
Load rejects an element whose id does not match its array's required prefix, which is the shape half of validation.
One shared decision for an entry point's activation, reused by the viewer, the coverage advisory and the eval.
The single definition of a well-formed code link: a file reference with an optional line, or a directory reference.

components.name: Fragment merge
components.purpose: Merges every worker's part of the map into one document. A box claimed by two workers stops the build, instead of one part quietly winning. Gives a worker the self-check it runs before handing its part back.

evidence.why: A duplicate id across two fragments is reported as a merge conflict naming both files, never silently overwritten.
Entry-point ids are minted here from content order, which is why a fragment must not author one.
The merged model is written to the canonical map file, plus its generated markdown view.
The per-fragment self-check runs the same row-local rules the whole-map validator does, in the authoring worker's own turn.

components.name: Map lookups
components.purpose: Reads one part of a map, so nobody opens the file and picks it apart by hand. Compares two versions of a map row by row, saying what was added, dropped or changed. Writes the note an operator leaves when accepting an advisory.

evidence.why: With no slice flag the whole parsed model is emitted, which is the read-only whole-map lookup.
For a row present on both sides, the fields whose values moved are recorded as the change.
One write for a whole batch of recorded lines, after every line has passed its shape check.
The single reader for a recorded line, so every advisory family parses the same key-and-reason shape.

components.name: Command shell and build setup
components.purpose: The single command every coyodex action runs through. Before a build starts, the command says which files will be read and which commit the map will name. The same command prints the brief one worker receives, and reads the list of code the map should skip.

evidence.why: Standard output is switched to line buffering at startup, so notes and failures interleave in program order under a pipe.
The up-front briefing is printed as plain text, with no exit-code signalling, for a person to read before the build.
Each accepted line of the analysis ignore file becomes an ordered rule, where a later rule overrides an earlier one.
Only the agent half of a contract template is printed, so the lead's own instructions cannot reach a worker.

components.name: Map validator
components.purpose: Checks a finished map is well formed before anyone trusts it. Every reference must resolve and every code link must point at a real file. Softer findings are advice, and an operator can silence one by writing down a reason.

evidence.why: A code link pointing at a file that is not there fails the map, rather than only nudging.
Warns when many sibling folders of code were folded into about one box on a diagram.
Counts what makes one sentence hard to read alone, and reports each count as advice.
Names the command that writes down a reason, once, where the operator reads the warnings.

components.name: Map auditor
components.purpose: Reads a map against itself and reports where the story and the mechanism disagree. Also ranks every claim the map makes about the code. Fresh readers then try to disprove the riskiest claims first.

evidence.why: Only a hard contradiction stops the build; every softer finding is advice to reconcile.
Access claims are ranked first, so the first batch of readers gets the riskiest claims.
A written reason silences exactly one finding, and the report still says what it silenced.
Clears its own earlier claim files, so a stale batch is never handed out a second time.

components.name: Diagram balance report
components.purpose: Counts the boxes on every diagram and says which screens are too crowded to read. Proposes a regrouping for each crowded screen, as a starting point for judgment. Never fails a build, because grouping is a view choice.

evidence.why: Warns when one screen shows more boxes than a reader can hold at once.
Writes a concrete regrouping suggestion for each crowded screen, ready to apply by hand.
Always reports success, because a crowded diagram is a judgement call and not a failure.
Reads the reasons an operator wrote down and skips the screens those reasons name.

components.name: Pre-commit gate run
components.purpose: Runs the other gates in one command and writes every finding to a report file. Says for each gate whether it really ran, so silence never reads as a pass. Can also name files that held an access check in an earlier map and hold none now.

evidence.why: A gate that should have run and did not makes the whole read incomplete, never a pass.
Writes every finding to a file, which trimming the screen output cannot hide.
Checks each piece of advice against what the map recorded, and names a missing record.
Names files that held an access check in an earlier map and hold none in this one.

components.name: Feature index
components.purpose: Joins every part of the map onto the feature it belongs to, and stores nothing. Also derives the one story order every feature screen draws. Counts what fails to join, so a partial list is never shown as a whole one.

evidence.why: Reuses the reader the Rules view uses, so the two screens cannot disagree about a rule.
Counts the decisions that reach no feature, so a floor is never read as an answer.
Derives one story order here, instead of letting the browser compute a layout.

components.name: Grounding record
components.purpose: Turns the fresh readers' verdicts into the four counts a map must carry before anyone trusts it. Those counts refuse a verdict for a claim nobody pinned, and a pinned claim nobody voted on. A second check compares a proven claim's code link against the line the fresh readers actually found.

evidence.why: One claim's votes are folded into one of three buckets, and the bucket totals become the counts the map ships.
A verdict about a claim the pinned worklist never held is refused, because the two sides came from different snapshots.
A pinned claim with no verdict is refused, unless the operator declares the pass deliberately partial.
The stored code link of a proven claim is compared against the lines the fresh readers reported.

components.name: Map repairs
components.purpose: Applies the mechanical corrections a map needs after a fresh reader reports, so none of them is hand-typed. A moved code link is rewritten, and a disproved relation is dropped. The happy-path steps that rode the dropped relation are healed too.

evidence.why: The corrected line the fresh readers agreed on is written into every drifted code link.
Dropping a disproved relation also removes the happy-path steps that rode it, so a rebuild cannot bring it back.
A relation declared at several different lines is reduced to the one occurrence the operator chose.
A text correction is written into the fragment that authored the row, so every later rebuild keeps it.

components.name: Assignment pass
components.purpose: Turns path rules into an explicit assignment file, so nobody lists hundreds of elements by hand. Every rule that matched nothing is named, and so is an assignment aimed at a group nobody declared. The build stamp is also written here, naming which conversation built the map and the code commit.

evidence.why: A rule whose path pattern reached no element is reported instead of quietly producing an empty assignment.
The expanded assignment file is written, keeping the repair decisions an earlier run had already recorded in it.
An assignment is applied to the merged map after the fragments are joined and before the map is written.
The session, the build minute and the code commit are written into the stamp file a commit is gated on.

components.name: Pre-index
components.purpose: Sizes a codebase before the map is drawn. The result gives the size and change rate of every folder. A symbol list says where every class and function is defined. The result also says how many parts a map of this size should hold.

evidence.why: Writes the sizing result, holding the folder weights, the symbol list, the import advisory and the part count.
The stop rule that turns one folder into one part of the map, which is how the advised count is reached.
Reads Python deeply through the standard parser, and every other language through an optional parser pack.
Records every file the tool could not read, so unread code is reported as unknown rather than as empty.

components.name: Change impact
components.purpose: Tells what a code change did to a finished map. The map is pinned to one commit, so the code has moved on. Two comparisons against that commit say which map boxes the changed lines belong to. The answer then spreads along the map's own arrows, so a reader sees everything the change touches.

evidence.why: Lists the files a change added, edited, deleted or renamed, including edits not yet committed.
Compares the two sides against the pinned commit, so a change already present at both ends counts as nothing.
Says how precisely a box was reached, from an exact line down to only the file, so the viewer never overstates precision.
Carries a hit outward along the map's own relations, so a reader sees everything the change touches.

components.name: Map server
components.purpose: Serves every remembered map to a browser on this machine. Each file shown comes from the project's history at the commit the map names.
components.depends_on: The diagram builder, the graph builder and the file browser tree.

evidence.why: sends a request for one project to that project's own handler
reads a file out of the project's history at the commit the map names
refuses any request that did not come from this machine
saves the list of project folders the landing page offers

components.name: Diagram builder
components.purpose: Builds every diagram a map's screens draw, straight from the map. The work happens on each request, so no diagram file is ever saved.
components.depends_on: The graph builder, and the map's own folder for the code links.

evidence.why: draws the whole map as boxes and arrows
draws one arrow for each pair of running processes that talk
draws one numbered message per step of a use case
folds the in-process libraries into one box on the top view

components.name: Graph builder
components.purpose: Turns the stored map into the boxes and arrows every screen draws. The same code writes the committed text version of the map.
components.depends_on: The stored map, plus the change-impact report when one sits beside it.

evidence.why: starts the committed text version with the map's title
turns one component of the map into a box a screen can draw
reads a change-impact report so the screens can badge what moved
writes the committed text version to disk

components.name: File browser tree
components.purpose: Builds the folder tree the file browser shows, marking which files the map covers. Also turns one file's change into the rows the code viewer paints.
components.depends_on: The graph builder, for the map's file anchors.

evidence.why: marks a file as covered by the map, or not covered at all
indexes every path the map points at, so a click finds its box
states on the tree what the ignore file hid from it
marks a line as added, for the side-by-side code view

components.name: Map canvas
components.purpose: Draws a map view as a diagram the reader can pan, zoom and click. Selecting a box or an arrow opens the card describing that box or arrow.

evidence.why: Turns the map's own diagram text into the drawing on screen.
Adds pan and zoom to the drawing, and keeps the reader's camera.
Gives each kind of view its own click behaviour on boxes and arrows.
Lights every selected element and dims the rest, so a selection reads as a focus.

components.name: Map reading pages
components.purpose: Draws the map screens that are pages of cards instead of drawings. The features, the rules, the storage, the tests and the glossary all live here.

evidence.why: The Features page leads with the story of every feature beside the cast of actors.
The Rules page groups the product's decisions into decision areas.
The Storage page is built from the stores the map records.
The Glossary page is a table of terms, not a drawing.

components.name: Trail and history
components.purpose: Decides which map screen is open, and names it in the tabs and the breadcrumb. Back and forward reopen a screen exactly as the reader left it.

evidence.why: Clicking a view tab opens that view.

components.name: Map quality score and verdict
components.purpose: Reduces a finished map to numbers that two runs can be compared on. Says whether the new map is as good as the accepted one, giving pass, drift or regressed. Also plants false claims about the map and counts how many a reviewer catches.

evidence.why: Counts the risky claims a reviewer is asked to check against the code.
One failed hard check makes the whole comparison read as regressed.
Turns the reviewers' votes into one pass rate, ignoring votes that failed.

components.name: Build transcript reader and spend report
components.purpose: Reads a finished build's chat log in slices, because the whole log is too big to open. Also reports the time and the money that build spent, per row of map produced.

evidence.why: Every record of one reply is folded into one turn, so ten tool calls at once count as one turn.
Lists every coyodex command the build ran, with the turn number that ran it.
Subtracts the stretches where nobody was working, so the clock measures the build.
Divides the spend by the rows of map produced, so two builds of different size compare.

components.name: Build behaviour scorecard
components.purpose: Scores what a build agent actually did against the rules the method sets. Reports a share of the chances the build had, never a pass or a fail. Also compares two scorecards to show which way each number moved.

evidence.why: A line with no chance to obey the rule scores as not applicable, never as zero.
Warns when a score rose only because the chances to break the rule vanished.
Refuses a map it cannot read, instead of quietly scoring less of the build.

components.name: Map archive and build guard
components.purpose: Moves a project's current map aside so the next run builds from scratch, keeping it as the baseline. Refuses a review while a build is still writing. Also stamps which chat built a map and bundles the two together.

evidence.why: Each archive takes the next number up, so the number always means how recent.
A recent write inside the map folder means something is still changing the map.
A chat file whose date moved counts as live only when a real message was added.
Refuses to move a map out of a repo when no chat could be bundled with it.

the first line of the map document's field-by-field specification

the command that prints a briefing, so nobody retypes one

subdomains.name: What a map holds

subdomains.purpose: Who uses the product, what they come to do, and the one walk that tells it end to end.

subdomains.name: The machine
subdomains.purpose: The parts the product is built from, what it pulls in from outside, and how the parts reach each other.

subdomains.name: The domain model
subdomains.purpose: The named types a project stores, their fields, how they relate, and the states they move through.

subdomains.name: Running and deciding
subdomains.purpose: What runs where, what is watched, what is configured, and every decision the product makes.

subdomains.name: The document and its record
subdomains.purpose: The whole map as one file, plus the citations and judgements that say how far it can be trusted.

subdomains.name: Building a map

subdomains.name: Proving a map

subdomains.name: What the viewer holds

subdomains.name: Judging a map

entities.name: RoleRelation

entities.name: Group

entities.meaning: A named box gathering members: a feature, a subsystem, a subdomain, or a decision area.

entities.name: Stake

entities.name: StoryAnchor
entities.meaning: Where a feature the main walk never reaches sits in the one product story.

entities.name: HappyStep
entities.meaning: One position in the ordered walk through the product's main story.

entities.name: Flow
entities.meaning: The inside view of one job, as an ordered run of interactions.

entities.name: FlowStep

entities.name: SubFlow

entities.name: Edge
entities.meaning: One backbone arrow: a piece of code reaching another, plus the calling line.

entities.name: EntryPoint
entities.meaning: One front door into the product, such as a route, a command, or a timed job.

entities.name: RunRow

entities.name: Store
entities.meaning: Where a type physically lives: which outside store, which compartment, in what shape.

entities.name: NonEntityType
entities.meaning: A named type left out of the domain model on purpose, carrying the reason why.

entities.name: StateMachine
entities.meaning: A lifecycle the code really implements: its states, its moves, and the declaring line.

entities.name: StateTransition
entities.meaning: One move from one state to another, plus the trigger that causes the move.

entities.name: MessagingRow

entities.name: VariantTag

entities.name: ConfigRow

entities.name: TestRow

entities.name: BusinessRule

entities.name: RuleSite

flows.title: Install the coyodex skill into the coding agents

steps.phrase: runs the install command in a fresh clone
checks the machine has Python 3.10 or newer
steps.note: stops with a plain message when Python is missing or older

steps.phrase: creates a private Python environment inside the clone, so nothing lands in the machine's own Python
installs coyodex into that private environment as an editable copy
steps.note: editable, so later edits need no reinstall

steps.phrase: reads the shipped skill file and replaces its placeholder with this clone's absolute path
writes the finished skill into the Claude Code skills folder
writes the same skill into the shared cross-agent skills folder Codex reads
prints one line per skills folder, naming the clone the installed skill now points at

flows.title: Start the local map server

steps.phrase: runs the start command, which serves the maps on the chosen port and opens the page
reads the port and the open-a-browser choice off the command line
reads the remembered project folders from the small file in the reader's home folder
steps.note: no disk scan — the served set is exactly this list

steps.phrase: loads each remembered project's map for its title, its goal and the commit it is pinned to
binds the server to the loopback address on that port, so only this machine can reach it
opens the landing page in the reader's default browser
steps.note: only when the start command asked for it

steps.phrase: sends the landing page, one self-contained document that pulls in no outside file
answers the page's request with one card per remembered project: its title, its pin, and whether its code can be read
writes the folder the reader adds back to that file, merging with what is on disk so a parallel writer is never lost
keeps answering requests until Ctrl-C, then says it stopped and closes the socket

flows.title: Open a project's map in a browser

steps.phrase: clicks a project card, which opens that project's own map address
sends the viewer shell, the same document for every project
fetches this map's whole view bundle before anything else on the page runs
turns every map element into a graph box carrying its name, its kind, its source line and its parent
turns every recorded relation into a graph arrow carrying its verb and its call site
renders that graph into one bundle holding every diagram, flow and colour
answers the fetch with the finished bundle, and keeps it for the next reader of the same map
copies the bundle into the page's own data, which every view below reads
opens the first view and records it as the first place in the trail
draws that view's diagram
wraps the drawing so the reader can pan it and zoom it
puts the drawn view on screen, ready to click into

flows.title: Report what a code change did to the map

steps.phrase: opens the dispatch rules to decide which mode this invocation is
runs the up-front briefing, before any mode is chosen
asks for the code paths that are changed but not committed
runs the version-control status command and returns the uncommitted paths
steps.note: coyodex's own folders are excluded, so its churn never makes the tree read as dirty

steps.phrase: prints the briefing: the file counts, the ignore patterns and what the pin will mean
reads the baseline map's pin, the commit the comparison starts from
compares the pin against the working tree and finds the code has moved on
steps.note: uncommitted edits count as moved on, and a dirty tree is the normal case here

steps.phrase: diffs the pin against the working tree, then adds the untracked files as added
steps.note: a plain diff omits untracked files, so they are listed separately

steps.phrase: asks the read-only reader which map element claims each changed file
steps.note: every change is placed at component level at least, and sharpened only where reading allows

steps.phrase: reads the element records and the edges into and out of each claiming element
follows those edges outward to the downstream elements and happy-path steps the change reaches
steps.note: the walk is redone from the diff every run; nothing precomputed is consulted

steps.phrase: hands back each touched element's exact was-to-now text, classified added, modified or deleted
steps.note: the report is written to disk and left uncommitted; the baseline itself changes only at accept

flows.title: Follow the product's story end to end

steps.phrase: opens this project's map page in the browser
joins every use case onto the feature it belongs to
walks the happy path to fix where each feature sits in the story
orders every feature into the one story column
clicks the Features tab
re-renders the page for the state the trail now points at
draws the Features page
shows one column holding every feature in story order, with the actors beside it
clicks the use-case pill on one feature's card
pushes that feature's own page onto the trail
lists that feature's use cases

flows.title: Read the code under a box

steps.phrase: clicks the code link a box shows
reads the component's source anchor, the line that code link names
steps.note: derived once, when the view bundle is built

steps.phrase: hands that file and line to the source column
colours the file's text with highlight.js
shows the file scrolled to the line the box named
opens the file browser to pick another file
asks for the repository's file tree at the map's commit
nests the commit's files into folders and marks the ones the map covers

flows.title: Open an element's source in the editor

steps.phrase: clicks the open-outside arrow beside the file the source column shows
reads the component's own files, the paths a source link points at
steps.note: derived once, when the view bundle is built

steps.phrase: derives the project's GitHub address from the repository's origin remote
asks the reader to pick an editor and confirm the repository root
steps.note: only the first time, before any source is opened outside

steps.phrase: opens the file at that line in the chosen editor through its URL scheme
opens the file on GitHub at the map's commit
steps.note: the fallback when no editor is chosen or its scheme is not allowed

flows.title: Brief the reader on what will be analysed

steps.phrase: runs the scope briefing on the repo before any other work
names each ignore pattern with the number of files it removed
steps.note: only when the ignore file holds at least one usable pattern

steps.phrase: warns when a folder inside the analysed set holds a previous map
steps.note: keyed on a folder that contains project-map.json or project-map.md, not on its name

steps.phrase: asks for the code paths that are changed but not committed
returns those paths, with coyodex's own output folders left out
reads HEAD's short sha and its date, for the commit the map will name
prints the file count, what each exclusion removed, and what the pin will mean
steps.note: the agent must show this text to the reader unchanged

flows.title: Declare code the map should not describe

steps.phrase: lists a fixture or vendored tree in the ignore file, one pattern per line
reads a leading exclamation mark as a negation, and skips blank and comment lines
drops a line that carries a trailing comment and reports it as unusable
steps.note: a hash opens a comment only at the start of a line, so `pattern  # why` is one literal pattern

steps.phrase: matches a wildcard-free pattern against that folder and everything beneath it
keeps the last rule that matched, so a later negation puts a file back
works out each folder's expected component count over the narrowed tree
says on every pre-index run how many files the patterns removed, and which pattern removed nothing
discloses the same per-pattern narrowing on every validate run
steps.note: unconditional, so the cheap check a lead runs most still carries the disclosure

flows.title: Size the code tree before choosing altitude

steps.phrase: runs the pre-index to weigh every folder before choosing the map's altitude
launches one git log pass and counts the commits that touched each file
adds each file's lines, its count and its churn into every folder above it
steps.note: the folders are then ordered heaviest first

steps.phrase: builds the parser for the file's language from the language pack
steps.note: Python is read with the standard library instead, so it needs no pack

steps.phrase: parses the file and collects every class and function definition with its line span
records each Symbol under its name, with its file, its kind and its line
works out how many components each folder should yield from its file count and size
turns the whole-tree expectation into a band, and says which cap decided it
writes the pre-index file with the weight tree, the symbols, the expectation and the coverage block
prints the counts, whether git and the parser pack were available, and the expected size
asks for the readable report of the pre-index it just wrote
prints the weight tree, the per-folder expectation and what the pre-index could not see

flows.title: Hand a fan-out worker its contract

steps.phrase: asks for the briefing one fan-out worker should receive, by name
resolves where the method and its briefings live, preferring the environment setting
reads the briefing file that name stands for
takes the quoted block as the worker's half, stripping the quote marker
otherwise takes everything after the single divider line
refuses a briefing with no boundary, rather than handing the lead's half to a worker
appends the writing rules for the briefings whose workers author map prose
prints only the worker's half, ready for the angle-bracket slots to be filled

flows.title: Self-check one harvested fragment

steps.phrase: runs the fragment self-check on the rows it has just written
builds a typed map document out of the fragment's JSON text
reads every row of the parsed map document
runs the shared row checks over code-link format, arrows, flow steps and business rules
checks that every code link names a file that exists in the project
asks which files are changed and not committed
steps.note: only when the fragment carries a commit pin with no dirty marker

steps.phrase: counts the code links pointing at a line that cannot be acting
reports the verdict line first, with the problem, warning and drift counts
prints each problem and each advisory row under the verdict

flows.title: Merge the workers' fragments into one map

steps.phrase: runs the merge, naming every fragment and the assignment file
asks which entity steps carry no backing arrow
adds the backbone arrow each of those steps implies, reading the verb off the step's own words
says it added the scratch folder to the ignore file, so the build never dirties the project
warns about a fragment left in the scratch folder that this run did not merge
prints the one-line digest of everything the merge changed

flows.title: Turn path rules into explicit assignments

steps.phrase: runs the assignment pass with a rules file and the folder of fragments
refuses a rules file holding a rule that assigns nothing
strips the line number off an element's code link, leaving the folder path a rule can match
matches one element's folder path against the rule's pattern
reads each front door's identifier together with its code link
steps.note: the code link is stored beside the identifier so a later renumber is caught

steps.phrase: names every rule that matched nothing and every rule pointing at a group nobody declared
prints how many rules were clean, matched nothing, or point at an undeclared group
writes the assignment file, carrying forward the directives it does not author

flows.title: Look up one part of the map

steps.phrase: runs the lookup, naming one file, one selector and one identifier
loads the named file, accepting a finished map or a half-written build fragment
asks the map document which element carries that identifier
reads that element's full stored record out of the map document
reads a front door's record, whose identifier is minted only when the map is merged
asks the serializer for the whole document when no selector is given
refuses, saying the identifier is not defined in the map
prints the answer as JSON

flows.title: Check the map is well formed

steps.phrase: asks for the check over the map it just wrote, with the repo-reading flags on
reads every element the map document declares, as the set a reference may name
reports every reference that names an element the map never defines
counts the long sentences and the missing link words in the map's plain text
fails the check when a code link names a file, or a line, the repo does not have
steps.note: only under the check-sources flag

steps.phrase: warns when a code link resolves to a line that cannot be the acting statement
steps.note: advisory, because the relation is usually real and only its line drifted

steps.phrase: walks the repo tree and names the folders no box on the map covers
steps.note: only under the check-coverage flag

steps.phrase: asks which screens hold more boxes than a reader can hold at once
prints the advisories, then the blocking problems, and exits non-zero when one stands

flows.title: Make the map's two layers refute each other

steps.phrase: asks for the two-layer comparison and for the ranked claims to be cut into batches
builds the walk's ordered steps and each step's entity reads and writes
records a finding when a walk step reads something the walk only writes later
blocks the run when a walk step explains itself by a step that comes after it
reports a flow whose opening actor is not one the use case declares
drops the advisories an operator recorded and names every one it dropped
steps.note: a contradiction is never dropped

steps.phrase: ranks each access decision and the line enforcing it at the top of the worklist
cuts the ranked claims into even batches, one file per theme, riskiest first
prints the findings and the ranked claims, exiting non-zero only on a contradiction

flows.title: Record an advisory the reader accepts

steps.phrase: asks to write down the reason one advisory was accepted, naming the heading and the line
refuses a line that names a key and states no reason
refuses a heading no check reads, and names the headings that are read
loads the fragment, remembering which sections it already held
appends the recorded line under the named heading, adding the section when it is missing
deletes one recorded line, and drops the whole heading when that was its last line
steps.note: the remove mode

steps.phrase: re-reads the lines it just added and refuses the whole batch when one adjudicates nothing
serializes the fragment once, with every line of the batch in it
says what was recorded, or that the fragment was left untouched

flows.title: Re-balance the diagrams against the traced graph

steps.phrase: asks how crowded each screen of the map is
reads every group and its parent, to build the child list of each screen
puts every component on the screen of the group it belongs to
counts the boxes on each screen and flags the crowded, the thin and the one-child ones
says how many screens sit inside the readable band
counts the arrows between components that cross from one group to another
proposes where a split of a crowded screen would fall, with the exact map change
prints the counts, the busiest seams and the proposals, and always exits clean
steps.note: grouping is a view choice, so the report never fails a build

flows.title: Disprove a claim against the code

steps.phrase: runs the audit and asks it to cut one claims file per theme
hands the auditor the batch directory and the per-batch cap
ranks every risky claim in the map into a work item carrying its anchor
refuses to cut any batch while the audit still holds a blocking contradiction
writes each theme's claims, anchors and details into their own batch file
steps.note: most dangerous theme first, split at the cap

steps.phrase: tells the lead to give each batch a fresh worker and to copy the briefing with a command
fills the briefing's four slots with the map, the repo, the batch id and its claims file
opens each claim's own anchor and reads the file the map points at
writes one answer per claim — confirmed, refuted or impossible to settle — with the true line
runs the answer-file check at the barrier, naming every batch it sent out
hands the check every answer file and the expected batch names
stops the barrier when an expected batch left no answer file behind
reports the files well formed and how many notes the evidence check could test

flows.title: Record what the skeptics proved

steps.phrase: runs the grounding write with the pinned claim list, every answer file and the built map
hands over the pinned claim list, the answer files and the map
re-derives the built map's live claim surface from the auditor's ranking
refuses the record when an answer names a claim the pinned list never held
refuses a pinned claim nobody voted on
steps.note: unless the run declares itself a partial pass with a note saying what was prioritized

steps.phrase: writes the four counts, the live claim digest and the note into the record
prints the counts the build's note must quote instead of retyping one
warns when the shipped map carries claims minted after the list was pinned
recomputes, per element, what the pass did to the claims that element makes
re-runs the validator over the map that now carries the record
blocks the map when confirmed, refuted and unsettled do not add up to challenged

flows.title: Correct a code link that points at the wrong line

steps.phrase: runs the drift check over the map with every answer file
hands the drift check the map and the answer files
re-derives the ranked claim list so every claim keeps the line the map stores
reports each confirmed claim whose stored line differs from the line the skeptics found
runs the repair, asking for the correction to be recorded rather than written into the map
hands the repair the map, the answer files and the reconcile file
asks for one truer line per drifted claim, at the line the skeptics settled on
records each claim and its corrected line in the reconcile file
steps.note: editing the built map instead would be undone by the next merge

steps.phrase: hands the corrected lines to the one writer both repair paths share
writes the corrected line onto the relation whose claim names it

flows.title: Drop a claim the code refutes

steps.phrase: runs the repair, asking to drop the refuted relation and record the drop for the next merge
hands the repair the map, the three parts of the relation and the reconcile file
refuses the drop when no relation in the map matches those three parts
records the drop, and how the riding walk steps should be healed, in the reconcile file
warns when walk steps ride the relation and the record says nothing about healing them
removes every relation matching the three parts
re-points or removes the walk steps that rode the dropped relation
names each walk step left with no backing relation when the record healed nothing

flows.title: Run the pre-commit read

steps.phrase: runs the pre-commit read over the map with every answer file
hands the gate run the map, the repo root and the answer files
refuses to start when the map cannot be loaded at all
runs the validator inside this same process, capturing both its streams
runs the auditor the same way and splits its findings into blocking and advisory
runs the drift check and the surviving-refutation check against the answer files
records one leg per gate, saying whether it ran and what it found
reports a leg it could have run but was not asked to, rather than staying silent
settles one verdict from the legs and hashes the map into the report
steps.note: a leg that failed forbids a clean verdict

steps.phrase: writes the whole finding list to a file beside the map, where a pipe cannot eat it
names the files that must be committed with the map, and the ones still missing
prints the verdict, the two counts, and which gates did not run

flows.title: Stamp which conversation built the map

steps.phrase: runs the stamp, pointing it at the build's header fragment
hands the stamp the repo, the mode and the header fragment
refuses when no session id is in the environment and none was passed
launches git for the short commit, its date and whether the tree holds uncommitted code
builds this session's entry — the id, the minute, the mode and the pinned commit
writes the record, replacing this session's own entry rather than adding a second
writes the same minute and the same pin into the header fragment
prints the minute on its own line so nothing has to be retyped
names the stamp command when the pre-commit read finds no record file

flows.title: See the change overlaid on the map

steps.phrase: asks what a code change did to the map, naming where the change starts and where it ends
steps.note: the request reaches the map server over the loopback address; the working tree is the default end point

steps.phrase: reads the symbol table saved beside the map, so an anchor can resolve to a whole definition
steps.note: an older map with no symbol table resolves every anchor at file level instead

steps.phrase: hands the map, its pinned commit and the two ends of the change to the impact engine
builds one anchor reference for every code link the map carries
launches git to list every file the change touched and to diff each one against the pinned commit
records one hit per anchor, saying whether the change reached its line, its definition or only its file
asks for every hit to be spread along the map's own relations, one hop only
answers with every part of the map the change reaches, what happened to it and how strongly it is reached

flows.title: Fold a change report into the map

steps.phrase: reads the accept instructions once the reader says the report is right
rewrites the map's rows from the report's was-to-now text, element by element
steps.note: accept re-reads no code: the report already carries the exact new text

steps.phrase: re-pins the map to the code commit it now describes
re-stamps who folded the report in and when, as an accept entry
writes this session's entry into the provenance file
rebuilds the pre-index at the new pin, so its file and line numbers match the re-pinned map
commits the map, its readable view, the pre-index and the report together

flows.title: Change the map by asking in plain words

steps.phrase: asks in plain words to split, rename, move or drill deeper into a part of the map
steps.note: a plain-words request is a direct map change, never a re-analysis of the code

steps.phrase: edits the named part of the map field by field, never by rebuilding it
rewrites a row's own text inside the fragment that authored it, so the edit survives the next merge
re-merges the edited fragments in a temporary copy first, refusing an edit that makes a row appear or vanish
names the field it rewrote and the fragment it wrote it in
drills deeper by retiring a leaf part, putting a group in its place and re-pointing every relation that named it
commits the edited map together with its regenerated readable view

flows.title: See what an edit changed, row by row

steps.phrase: asks what changed between the map before an edit and the map after it
steps.note: the two maps must be two writes of the same work, never two independent builds

steps.phrase: loads each of the two map files as a map document, refusing one that is malformed
asks which arrays carry an authored identifier, so those rows are matched by identifier
steps.note: relations and entry points are matched on their own text instead, because their identifiers are minted afresh on every write

steps.phrase: lists the rows dropped and the rows added in each array
names each surviving row that changed, with the exact fields that moved
flags an identity held by more than one row and reports it by count instead of pairing the rows
prints the same answer as data when asked for it

flows.title: Score a rebuilt map against the accepted one

steps.phrase: runs the scoring command with the new map and the accepted baseline
reads the accepted map's stored quality signals out of the baseline folder
steps.note: a baseline folder that is missing or holds no signals stops the run instead of reporting nothing got worse

steps.phrase: turns the frozen map file into the typed document
counts the map's well-formedness problems and warnings
counts the map's contradictions, advisories and risky claims
records the counted quality signals of the new map
settles on pass, drift or regressed from every hard check and band
prints the verdict with the checks and the bands that moved

flows.title: Have judges read both maps

steps.phrase: asks for the riskiest claims one map makes
steps.note: run once for the new map and once for the accepted one

steps.phrase: checks whether a stored judgement was made under the current judging protocol
reads the fingerprint recorded with the stored judgement
steps.note: a different model, skeptic count, sample cap or rubric makes the stored judgement unusable

steps.phrase: hands back one row per skeptic vote plus each judge's rubric scores
re-reads the frozen map so every vote is matched against the same document
records the pass rate, the excluded failures and the median rubric scores
prints how many claims held up and the overall score

flows.title: Accept a run as the new baseline

steps.phrase: takes the map's freeze hash before anything scores it
scores the older accepted map so it can serve as the baseline
reads a map an older coyodex wrote, after dropping the block that no longer exists
steps.note: only for reading; every writing path still refuses an out-of-date map

steps.phrase: archives the finished run, handing back the freeze hash
refuses the whole run when the map no longer matches its freeze hash
steps.note: only when the map was edited after the hash was taken

steps.phrase: renders the map's readable view into the run folder
writes the run's counted quality signals into the run folder
writes the judged pass rate and rubric scores beside them
promotes that run folder to the baseline
reports the baseline now holds the map, its view, its signals and its judgement

flows.title: Measure how many planted falsehoods the skeptics catch

steps.phrase: asks for the riskiest claims, to use as the batch to corrupt
asks for ten planted falsehoods, spread evenly across the four shapes
writes the corrupted batch and, beside it, the answer key naming every planted claim
hands back the skeptics' verdicts on the corrupted batch
reports how many planted falsehoods were caught, shape by shape
steps.note: a moved anchor counts as caught on the evidence line the skeptic found, never on the verdict

flows.title: Refuse to review a build that has not finished

steps.phrase: runs the pre-check before reviewing a finished build
reads the recorded build stamp and takes its session list
takes the newest recorded session as the build being reviewed
refuses the review and tells the developer to open a new chat
steps.note: when the newest recorded session is this very chat, so the review would read the file it is writing

steps.phrase: refuses the review and names the file that just changed
steps.note: when anything under .coyodex/ was written in the last three minutes; the stamp is written near the end of a build and the build keeps going after it

steps.phrase: refuses the review and names the other chat that is still writing
steps.note: only a chat whose newest real message is recent counts as live; a file merely touched does not

steps.phrase: clears the review, naming the build's chat and the minute it was built

flows.title: Read a build transcript in slices

steps.phrase: asks which chat built this map
loads the recorded build stamp
walks every recorded session, reading its build minute, its mode and its chat id
prints the recorded sessions, newest last, so the build's chat id can be turned into a log path
runs the transcript reader on that chat's log with no range asked for
prints one line per tool call with its turn number, counting every record of one reply as one turn
asks for one turn range, because the whole log is far too big to open
lists every coyodex command the build ran inside that range, with the turn that ran it
counts the tools used and the size of each fan-out inside that range

flows.title: Score a build's behaviour against the method

steps.phrase: opens the retrospective on a build that has already finished
sends the developer into the retrospective recipe, which names the scorecard command
runs the scorecard on the build's chat log, naming the map that build produced
refuses before scoring anything, saying which rules would have stopped measuring
steps.note: only when a map was named and cannot be read

steps.phrase: asks the reader for the build's turns, every record of one reply folded into one turn
loads the built map, so the rules whose subject is the map can be checked against it
saves the scorecard beside the chat log, so a later build can be compared against this one
prints one line per rule: how many chances the build had, and how many it took
steps.note: a rule the run gave no chance to reads as not applicable, never as zero

steps.phrase: later asks it to compare two saved scorecards
prints each rule before and after, which way it moved, and a warning when a score rose only because the chances vanished

flows.title: Measure what a build spent

steps.phrase: runs the spend report on the build's chat log, naming the map that build produced
bounds the report to the build's own turns
steps.note: a chat keeps answering questions after the map lands, and those turns are not the build

steps.phrase: counts every row of the produced map, the divisor the whole report is stated against
reports the wall clock of the run and the active time, with the stretches nobody was working cut out
reports the tokens and the money, one row per kind of worker and a total across the lead chat and every worker chat
reports the money and the seconds per row of map, so two builds of different size compare
warns that the numbers cover the lead chat alone
steps.note: when no worker chat logs sit beside the session, which is about four fifths of a fan-out build's spend

flows.title: Archive a map so the next run builds from scratch

steps.phrase: runs the archive command on the mapped repo before starting a rebuild
moves the map document, with the rest of the build output, into the next numbered archive folder
steps.note: moved rather than deleted, because the old map is the baseline the new one is compared against

deployment.runs_on: the user's own machine, in a private Python environment inside the coyodex folder
deployment.exposed_as: a terminal command, started by hand or by the coding agent following the method
deployment.config_source: The package file declares the command name. The setup target builds the environment and installs the package editable, so the clone stays the live source.

deployment.runs_on: the same machine, as a long-running Python process bound to the loopback address only
deployment.exposed_as: a web address on port 8765, reachable from that machine and no other
deployment.config_source: The port comes from the start option, defaulting to 8765. The projects served come from the recents file in the user's home folder; there is no disk scan.

deployment.exposed_as: the landing page the map server serves, showing one card per project
deployment.config_source: Per-machine choices kept by the browser itself: the chosen editor, the project's folder on disk, and the code-hosting address. Defaults for the last two are delivered with the map.

observability.where_emitted: The check command prints an inventory line, then the warnings, then the blocking failures. A machine-readable flag prints the same findings as data, with no list shortened.
observability.where_viewed: The terminal of whoever ran the check, usually the coding agent building the map.
observability.alerts: None. A blocking failure is reported as a non-zero exit, which stops the build step that ran the check.

observability.signal: Map server start and stop lines
observability.where_emitted: On start the server prints how many projects it has and the address it listens on. On stop it prints one line.
observability.where_viewed: The terminal the map server runs in.

observability.where_emitted: Nothing. The map server deliberately silences the request log it would otherwise print.
observability.where_viewed: Nowhere. There is no request history to read.

observability.where_emitted: The map server checks its own Python files while it runs. When one is newer than the start time it prints a warning saying to restart.
observability.where_viewed: The terminal the map server runs in. The warning appears once per change, not once per request.

observability.where_emitted: Each build records its session id and its build time in a provenance file inside the project's map folder.
observability.where_viewed: That file. The finalize step refuses to bless a commit whose provenance file is missing.

observability.where_emitted: A change-impact run writes a markdown report next to the map in the project's map folder.
observability.where_viewed: The file itself, and the viewer, which lays the report over the map when the file is present.
